BRB1.claim: Ranthambore National Park, 14 km from Sawai Madhopur, covers 392 sq km between the Aravallis and Vindhyas and is home to tigers and over 300 bird species.

evidence.quote: Situated 14 km from Sawai Madhopur, the Ranthambore Park gets its name from the Ranthambore Fort situated within its boundaries.
The National Park, situated amidst the Aravalis and Vindhya ranges is spreads over an area of 392 sq.km of thick forest punctuated with pleasant waterfalls.
It is home to the elusive tiger, other animals found here include chinkara, sambhar, cheetal and over 300 species of birds.

BRB2.claim: A safari is the best way to see Ranthambore's tigers, sloth bears and leopards; book on the Rajasthan wildlife website.

evidence.quote: One of the best ways to observe wildlife at the Ranthambore National Park is through a safari.
Apart from the royal Bengal tiger, you can also spot sloth bears, leopards, jackals, foxes and hyenas.
For information & online reservations, visit: http://www.rajasthanwildlife.rajasthan.gov.in/bookTrip.do

BRB3.claim: Sawai Madhopur has regular trains; Jaipur airport, 150–170 km away, is the closest.

evidence.quote: You can easily get regular trains to Sawai Madhopur from other major cities of the country.
The Jaipur Airport is the closest and is located 150-170 kilometres away.

BRTB_SEAS.claim: Ranthambore National Park is open to visitors from 1 October to 30 June; the core zones close for the monsoon from July to September.

evidence.quote: Ranthambore National Park opens its gates to visitors from October 1st to June 30th every year.
Core zones are closed from July to September.

BRTB_TIME.claim: Ranthambore runs a morning and an afternoon safari; in December and January they run 7–10:30 am and 2–5:30 pm, and from April to June the morning slot starts around 6 am.

evidence.quote: In December and January, safaris run 7:00 AM–10:30 AM (morning) and 2:00 PM–5:30 PM (evening)
From April to June, morning safaris start around 6:00 AM and run to 9:30 AM

BRTB_TATK.claim: Last-minute Tatkal safari seats, for the coming seven days, open for booking daily at 11 am.

evidence.quote: Tatkal safaris for seven days ahead open daily at 11:00 AM.

evidence.quote: The noteworthy Ranthambore Fort was built by the Chauhan rulers in the 10th century.
The fort is characterised by temples, tanks, massive gates and huge walls.

BRBF2.claim: The Trinetra Ganesh temple inside the fort holds a fair on Bhadrapad Chaturthi.

evidence.quote: Every year a fair is held on Chaturthi of Bhadrapad month.

RN1.claim: Ranthambore was once the private game reserve of the royal house of Jaipur.

evidence.quote: Once a private game reserve of the royal House of Jaipur

RN2.claim: Besides tigers, look for sloth bear, leopard, caracal, jackal, hyena, chital, sambar and nilgai; the Indian wolf is seen occasionally.

evidence.quote: Apart from the tiger, you can also spot sloth bear, leopard, caracal, jackal, fox, hyena and mongoose at Ranthambore.
The elusive Indian wolf too, has been spotted here occasionally.
The dainty chital, sambhar deer, the blue bull antelope or nilgai, rhesus macaque, langur

evidence.quote: covering 1,334 square kilometres while housing 392 square kilometres of the pristine national park

Though she passed away in August 2016

such as Padam Talao, Malik Talao, and Raj Bagh Talao

evidence.quote: As of 2022, there were 69 tigers in the national park.

RN9.claim: The fort is good for birdwatching, with langurs and, near water, sometimes the fishing cat.

overview.text:
Ranthambore National Park, 14 km from Sawai Madhopur, was once the private game reserve of the royal house of Jaipur. Its 392 sq km park, part of a 1,334 sq km tiger reserve between the Aravallis and Vindhyas, is dry dhonk forest broken by lakes such as Padam Talao, old pavilions like Jogi Mahal and the Rajbagh ruins; there were 69 tigers as of 2022, and the tigress Machli made it famous worldwide.

Safaris run morning and afternoon in jeeps and canters, booked on the Rajasthan wildlife website, and the park is open from 1 October to 30 June. Above the forest rises 10th-century Ranthambore Fort, part of the UNESCO-listed Hill Forts of Rajasthan, with the Trinetra Ganesh temple inside. Jaipur airport is about 150–170 km away; trains stop at Sawai Madhopur.
